To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the membrane proximal region of VEGFR2 interacts with non-phosphorylate β3 integrin, while phosphorylation of the membrane proximal tyrosine residue in β3CT enhances the binding to VEGFR2, which is important for VEGF-induced endothelial cell signaling and angiogenesis.
phosphorylation of the integrin β3 tail regulates its binding to VEGFR2, and this interaction is required for VEGF-induced endothelial cell signaling and angiogenesis.
the membrane-proximally located tyrosine residue in VEGFR is required for its interaction with integrin β3 and this interaction is enhanced when this tyrosine is phosphorylated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the interaction between integrin and tyrosine kinase receptors and the role of phosphorylation in this interaction.
the role of phosphorylation in integrin signaling, specifically the role of β3 phosphorylations in VEGF signaling.
the mechanism of integrin and Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR-2) cross-talk in endothelial cell signaling and angiogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
integrin β3 crosstalk with VEGF2R accommodating tyrosine phosphorylation as a regulatory switch.
phosphorylation of integrin β3 at Y747 enhances the interaction between integrin β3 and VGF receptor 2.
the phosphorylated Y747 of β3CT mediates the binding of β3CT to the 801YLS motif of VEGFR2, thereby enhancing the VEGF-induced activation of VEGFR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phosphorylation of β integrin is required for VEGFR2 signaling and VEGFR signaling is required for β integrin activation.
β3 phosphorylation is a regulatory switch in the interaction between β integrin and VGEFR2.
β3 integrin phosphorylated at 747Y is a key regulatory switch that modulates the cross talk between β3 integrins and VEGFR-2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phosphorylation of β integrin at Y747 can be used as a regulatory switch to modulate the cross talk between integrin and its binding partners.

phosphorylated integrin β3CT is required for VEGF-induced endothelial signaling and angiogenesis, suggesting that integrin β3 phosphorylation could be a therapeutic target for antiangiogenic treatment of cancer and other angiogenesis dependent diseases.
the membrane proximal motif in VEGFR is a binding site for integrin β3CT.
